doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Kind of Blue business and anniversary tours
title: Wallace Roney and Miles
summary: Cobb says Wallace was Miles's protege and how he told Miles about the boxer's son.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom

blocks.x: But in that circumstance, not only with Esperanza, but probably to a degree with Giovan[ni Hidalgo], and probably to a degree with – although Vincent [Herring] was with you with Nat, and he had the benefit of that, but you got to have – or, there’s an opportunity there, that you have, and that they have, to get a little something that . . .

Yeah. I can make it real, because I was original. So that’s one plus. And the reason we had Wallace [Roney] there, because he would probably have been Miles’s choice, because they were tight. They were buddies. That’s Wallace’s mentor, is Miles.

This is a little aside. I started working with Wallace when he was in high school. I’ve been in his house when Miles called. His daddy, Big Wally, and I couldn’t believe this stuff, I should say. He’d be like, “Little Wally! Miles is on the phone.” I thought, my – you all got to be kidding. So that went on a long time.
I think I remember telling Miles. I say, “I got this little guy from my hometown that plays trumpet, and his daddy is a boxer.” So that right there piqued his interest right away.
Yeah. Somewhere down the line they – all that stuff came together, and they got together. I told him. I say, “Yeah, they got a little trumpet player, and his daddy used to – is a boxer.”

He was like a jazz – I would call him – you got stage mothers. He was – meaning theatrical stage mothers. He was a jazz dad. He was a jazz stage dad. And he got it not only with Wallace, but with Antoine [Roney]. Got that from filming.
